text: The two operations that carry the legacy AgentStepClient across the boundary are this key's: POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-steps for the step itself and PUT /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId}/decision-record for the link between the run and the record, with the legacy request members agentCode, caseId, decisionCode, stepKey, ruleResult and inputs and the legacy outcome members decisionLogEntryId, appliedResult, recommendation, fallback, fallbackReason, autonomyMode and agentRunId. No other operation is added to the eleven P10 operations and none of them is changed.
why: The legacy published interface is a Java call (AgentStepClient.runStep) and the eleven operations of TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 hold no run-submit and no link, so the boundary the legacy section 12 spans has no method and no path in any source.
read: Legacy RWB-TE-013 section 12; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16; Template and Rules v1 §R4 (base per service) and §R5.5 DP-11, DP-13 and DP-20
confirm: Solution architect with the tech lead of rwb-agent at the wave 1 contract freeze.
impact: If a different path or a single operation is agreed, only the path and the operation count in the contract, the fakes and the route change; the request and answer members, the idempotency rule and the record payload do not.

text: The step operation is the single recorded exception to the 2 s client budget of DP-11: its budget is agent_policy.timeout_seconds, which is 60 seconds in the legacy policy 'P1' and never more than the policy allows, because the run is started and awaited at the boundary and NFR-010 allows the full wait before the rule result is used. Every other REST hop of the service keeps the 2 s budget.
why: DP-11 fixes one hop with a 2 s client budget for a published interface, agent_policy.timeout_seconds is 60 with the rule result used on expiry (R-UNI-32), and NFR-010 allows 60 seconds for an answer; no source reconciles the two waits.

confirm: Solution architect with the owners of rwb-agent and of the calling services at the wave 1 contract freeze.
impact: If the boundary must answer inside 2 s, the step becomes an accepted submission whose outcome is read back through the run read, and every calling step's flow changes; the run, the record and the fallback do not.

text: The call type between a calling step and rwb-agent is not fixed by any source. This story and its contract fix the REST face with a mock, one hop and the policy timeout, and RWB-ITG-TE013-ITG proves the real hop across services, where the client starts AgentRunWorkflow on queue rwb-agent. Both readings keep the same request, the same outcome, the same step key as workflow identity and idempotency key, and the same record write by the calling step.
why: Architecture v5 slide 16 shows the run as AgentRunWorkflow on the rwb-agent queue, Template and Rules DP-11 and DP-20 make the legacy in-process call a REST contract with a mock, and no source fixes which of the two the seam uses.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16 and 41; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-10, DP-11 and DP-20; Legacy RWB-TE-013 section 4; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.1
confirm: Solution architect with the owners of rwb-agent and of the calling services, with the harness of RWB-ITG-TE013-ITG.
impact: If the seam is the Temporal child only, the provided operations reduce to the reads and the link and the contract keeps the request and answer shapes as the workflow's input and output; the fallback, the record and the tests do not change.

text: The decision record of a step is written by the calling step through the local decision-record library in its own schema and transaction, published as EV-08 on rwb.decision-record.v1, and never by an agent run; rwb-agent stores the record reference on agent_run.decision_log_id through the link operation, once per run. The legacy decision-log mapping is kept as the payload mapping, with the agent version string '<agent>@<policy>/<prompt>' and the actions {agentRunId, mode, fallback, fallbackReason} plus the case ID. The gateway-bff route in front of the run read is a pass-through of one hop whose name and path are agreed with the route contract of RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and no screen reaches rwb-agent directly.
why: The legacy client wrote the P7 entry itself and then linked it to the run, DP-03 moves the writer to a local library and the topic, the baseline contract of RWB-P10-E1058-CON states that the record of a step is written by the step, DP-19 requires a composite route for a screen read and no source names the agent admin route.

text: The per-service login of rwb-agent under DP-02 is not named by any source; the stories name it 'the rwb-agent login (DP-02)' and 'the rwb-agent service identity', with grants on schema rwb_agent only and the naming taken from the platform at build time. The calling module keeps its own service identity, and the legacy identities SY-CASEWF, SY-AGENT and SY-DECLOG are kept as legacy references only.
why: Template and Rules §R4 and DP-02 require one login per service, TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T6.2 speaks of service identities for jobs and agents, and the legacy section 3 names only SY-CASEWF, SY-AGENT and SY-DECLOG.

text: The contract fixes the two operation paths, the JSON spelling of the legacy members and their types: ruleResult as {ruleId, ruleVersion, toState, result} with result as free JSON, inputs as a map of masked values, confidence and cost as decimals of four places, and each refusal as the platform problem response with its status, code and detail. The legacy Java member names are the source of the JSON names and no member is dropped.
why: The legacy section 12 gives Java records, TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 gives no run-submit operation, and no source states the JSON shape, the decimal scale or the detail text of a refusal for these operations.

text: The refusal set of the step operation is 401 without a session or a service identity, 403 without the Rules and parameters right with MSG-P4-002, 409 for a repeated step key whose first run is still RUNNING and for a link where the run already holds another record, 422 for a request the service cannot accept with MSG-GEN-001, and 503 when the store, the workflow or a consumed contract is unavailable. A repeat of a step key whose first outcome is written answers 200 with that outcome, which is the legacy rule R-UNI-40.
why: The legacy interface throws one exception and the legacy repeat rule returns the first outcome, while the platform uses a status-code set; no source says how a repeat that arrives while the first run is in flight is answered.

impact: If a concurrent repeat must instead be waited on, its status changes from 409 to 200 and the caller's retry logic changes; the stored run and record do not.

text: The record reference the outcome carries and the link stores is the identifier the decision-record library returns, a UUID, and the record itself is read back through GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId} of rwb-decision with a Decision log R right; the run and the record are joined by that reference only, with no foreign key across a schema.
why: The legacy interface returns decisionLogEntryId as a UUID and DF-AGT-058 decision_log_id is a CROSS_REF uuid, while the record type, the ledger and the read-back belong to rwb-decision and no source gives the reference shape for this key.
